title: Disappointing, not for tomato juice?
text: Disappointing, not for tomato juice?. Started my canning season this year and found my trusty old Foley food mill had finally wore out after a couple of decades. Found this, went with it as most were either out of stock or prices were ridiculous. I will say that the metal is thick. To assemble, you put the bottom plate in and put the handle piece on top. Sit down so you can have the pressure to be able to get the spring to compress to get the bar in place (at least I had to). Cooked my tomatoes down and put in the mill. As you can see in the picture, there is a gap between the plate and the fin. It does not do tomatoes for juice. I attempted now twice. So to use this, I had to mash my tomatoes down, ladle as much through and then use a flat spatula to compress the tomatoes to the wall of the mill to actually get most of the juice out. That's the second image, sorry not any better, but it's just to show a LOT of juice was lost from this mill. I would say, if you need one and not using to extract juice, you may be okay. Outside of that, good luck!
